topicTitle: Acceleration as a Rate of Change

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from \(-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(9\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average acceleration.
For \(v_x(t)=2t+5\), find \(a_x\).
A velocity-time graph is horizontal. What is the acceleration?
questions.answer:
A horizontal velocity-time graph has zero slope:
\[
a_x=0
\]

questions.prompt: For \(x(t)=t^2\), find \(a_x\).
For \(v_x(t)=12-4t\), find \(a_x\). Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\)?
questions.answer:
\[
a_x=-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}
\]
At \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\),
\[
v_x=8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Velocity and acceleration have opposite signs, so the speed is decreasing.

questions.prompt: Velocity changes from \(-10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average acceleration and say whether speed increased.
A particle has \(v_x=-6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(a_x=-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Is its speed increasing or decreasing?
questions.answer: The velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the speed is increasing.

questions.prompt: What are the SI units of acceleration?
questions.answer:
Acceleration is velocity change per time:
\[
a_x=\frac{\Delta v_x}{\Delta t}
\]
So the SI unit is \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

questions.prompt: On a velocity-time graph, what does acceleration represent?
questions.answer:
Acceleration is the slope of the velocity-time graph:
\[
a_x=\frac{dv_x}{dt}
\]

questions.prompt: For \(v_x(t)=6t-t^2\), find \(a_x(t)\).
Velocity is \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at the start and \(5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at the end of a \(10\,\mathrm{s}\) interval. Find average acceleration.
For \(v_x(t)=3t^2-2t\), find \(a_x\) at \(t=1\,\mathrm{s}\).
If \(v_x(t)=8\), what is \(a_x\)?
Velocity changes by \(18\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) over \(6\,\mathrm{s}\). Find average acceleration.
For \(x(t)=t^3\), find \(a_x\) at \(t=2\,\mathrm{s}\).
Does negative acceleration always mean the object is slowing down?
questions.answer: No. The speed decreases only when velocity and acceleration have opposite signs. If both are negative, the speed increases.

questions.prompt: If \(a_x=0\), what can be said about velocity in one-dimensional motion?
questions.answer: The velocity is constant. The position changes linearly with time.

questions.prompt: A particle has \(v_i=15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(a_x=-3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) for \(4\,\mathrm{s}\). Find \(v_f\).
A particle has \(a_x=-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) for \(5\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its velocity change.
A particle has \(v_x(t)=t^3-6t^2+8t\). Find the intervals where the particle is speeding up for \(t\geq0\).
questions.answer:
\[
a_x=3t^2-12t+8
\]
Speeding up occurs when \(v_x\) and \(a_x\) have the same sign. The zeros are
\[
v_x=t(t-2)(t-4)
\]
\[
a_x=0\Rightarrow t=2\pm\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{3}
\]
Use these critical times to test signs on each interval; keep the intervals where \(v_xa_x>0\).

questions.prompt: A velocity changes uniformly from \(-12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(6\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the acceleration, the time when the particle stops, and the displacement over the interval.
